title: Groundhog_Backdoor_Investigation_45d
description: Investigate and respond to the Groundhog backdoor malware incident in your network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Groundhog backdoor malware has been detected in your network. This malware targets Linux servers, uses XOR encryption for communication, and can perform DDoS attacks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can access the `next-target` host using SSH. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can access the `next-target` host using SSH. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the `target` host. The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`. To identify it, check the running services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized. This helps in understanding the malware's persistence and execution mechanism. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Check running services
hints.content: Start by listing all running services. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to see the services.

hints.title: Look for unusual services
hints.content: Review the list of services and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized. Pay attention to service names and descriptions.

hints.title: Identify the suspicious service
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to confirm its presence.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The flag type is a persistence mechanism.
levels.solution: The persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service is a systemd timer. To investigate this, use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. This helps in understanding how the malware ensures its continuous operation across reboots. The flag type is a persistence mechanism.

hints.title: Understand persistence mechanisms
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms are methods used by malware to ensure it runs automatically after a system reboot. Common mechanisms include systemd timers, cron jobs, and startup scripts.

hints.title: Investigate systemd timers
hints.content: Systemd timers are a common persistence mechanism. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Identify the systemd timer
hints.content: The persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service is a systemd timer. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to confirm its presence.

levels.title: Locate Executable File
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity. The flag type is a file path.
levels.solution: The path to the script that the suspicious service executes is `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`. To locate it, check the service unit file using the command `cat /etc/systemd/system/bkd.service`. This helps in identifying the malicious payload and understanding its functionality. The flag type is a file path.

hints.title: Understand service unit files
hints.content: Service unit files contain information about the services, including the executable or script they run. Use the command `cat /etc/systemd/system/bkd.service` to view the service unit file.

hints.title: Look for the executable path
hints.content: Review the service unit file and look for the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the executable or script path. Pay attention to the path and filename.

hints.title: Identify the executable file
hints.content: The path to the script that the suspicious service executes is `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`. Use the command `cat /etc/systemd/system/bkd.service` to confirm its presence.
